245	      <ItemVariantProvider variant={product}>
246	        {showLoading && <LoadingSpinner />}
247	        <Stack layerStyle="cardBordered" align="flex-start" {...containerStyles}>
248	          <Flex sx={styles.row} width="full" backgroundColor="white">
249	            <CartItemVariantImage />
250	            <Stack sx={styles.details} flex={1}>
251	              <Flex sx={styles.info}>
252	                <Stack spacing={1}>
253	                  <CartItemVariantName />
254	                  <CartItemVariantAttributes excludeBonusLabel combineAttributeValues />
255	                  <HideOnDesktop>
256	                    <Box marginTop={2}>
257	                      <CartItemVariantPrice align="left" currency={activeCurrency} />
258	                    </Box>
259	                  </HideOnDesktop>
260	                </Stack>
261	                {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
262	                  <HideOnMobile>{deliveryActions}</HideOnMobile>
263	                )}
264	              </Flex>
265	
266	              {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
267	                <HideOnDesktop>{deliveryActions}</HideOnDesktop>
268	              )}
269	
270	              <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">
271	                <Stack spacing={1}>
272	                  {!hideStepperAndActions &&
273	                    !(isRemoving && product.bonusProductLineItem) &&
274	                    (product.bonusProductLineItem ? (
275	                      <BonusProductQuantity product={product} />
276	                    ) : (
277	                      <ProductQuantityPicker
278	                        product={product}
279	                        onItemQuantityChange={onItemQuantityChange}
280	                        stepQuantity={stepQuantity}
281	                        quantity={quantity}
282	                        setQuantity={setQuantity}
283	                      />
284	                    ))}
285	                </Stack>
286	                <Stack>
287	                  <HideOnMobile>
288	                    <CartItemVariantPrice currency={activeCurrency} />
289	                  </HideOnMobile>
290	                  {!hideStepperAndActions && <HideOnMobile>{primaryAction}</HideOnMobile>}
291	                </Stack>
292	              </Flex>
293	
294	              {/* SFCC-795 (plan step 3.3): discount label, directly beneath the stepper/price row
295	                  above, ahead of the inline message below — prop-driven only, no empty node when
296	                  omitted. See the `discountLabel` prop's own JSDoc for the styling citation. */}
297	              {discountLabel && (
298	                <ZimmInlineMessage variant="success" text={discountLabel} dataTestId="zimm-discount-label" />
299	              )}
300	
301	              {/* SFCC-795 §11.2: sits between the stepper (above) and the actions row (the
302	                  existing inventory Box below, secondaryActions, and the mobile primaryAction
303	                  block further down) — prop-driven only, see this file's own docblock. */}
304	              {message && <ZimmInlineMessage variant={message.variant} text={message.text} />}
305	
306	              <Box>
307	                {product && showInventoryMessage && (
308	                  <Fade in={true}>
309	                    <Text color="orange.600" fontWeight={600}>
310	                      {inventoryMessage}
311	                    </Text>
312	                  </Fade>
313	                )}
314	              </Box>
315	
316	              {!hideStepperAndActions && secondaryActions}
317	            </Stack>
318	          </Flex>
319	
320	          {!hideStepperAndActions && (
321	            <HideOnDesktop>
322	              <Box w={'full'}>{primaryAction}</Box>
323	            </HideOnDesktop>
324	          )}
325	        </Stack>
326	      </ItemVariantProvider>
327	    </Box>
328	  );
329	};
330	
331	export default ProductItem;

2	 * Recipe — cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2).
3	 * `.claude/session-notes.md` §11.2: "inline message (error/warning) sits between the stepper and
4	 * the actions, w-full, `Default/Caption` regular 12px / lh18. In error states the Item Details
5	 * gap widens 12 -> 16px." (the gap widening is `ZimmCartItem`'s own `hasError` resolution prop —
6	 * see product-item.css.ts — not this recipe's concern; this file owns only the message's own
7	 * type/colour/icon.)
8	 *
9	 * Two-part multipart recipe (`root`/`text`), following zimmDrawer.css.ts's plain-object
10	 * `{parts, baseStyle, variants}` shape rather than `defineStyleConfig` — no Chakra helper
11	 * factory, same Chakra-native string `variants` resolution either form supports.
12	 *
13	 * Restructured from a single-node `defineStyleConfig` (SFCC-795 rework — Marcel's own visual
14	 * checkpoint against the real Figma file surfaced a genuine gap the original single-node shape
15	 * couldn't express): the `warning` variant carries a leading 16x16 icon, the `error` variant
16	 * never does. This was already a known requirement, not something discovered fresh at the
17	 * checkpoint or borrowed from an unrelated ticket — `.claude/session-notes.md:395` (the original
18	 * SFCC-795 ticket restatement, written before any Figma metadata was pulled) already says
19	 * "warning state (grey info icon + message, e.g. 'Maximum purchase quantity reached for this
20	 * size')", the exact copy string used here. It was simply dropped somewhere between that
21	 * restatement and the written build plan's step 3.2 text, and the checkpoint is what caught it.
22	 *
23	 * Confirmed against 3 real cart-item instances in Figma file QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs
24	 * ("Zimmermann_Designs") — the two error-copy states (FULLY OOS node 9323-101979, PARTIAL OOS
25	 * node 9323-98397) have a bare `<text>` message sub-tree, no icon; the warning-copy state's own
26	 * "Cart Item" instance is `icon(16x16, x=0) -> 8px gap -> text(x=24)`. That instance is node
27	 * 9323:106685, named "Cart Item" — confirmed via its own metadata to be one of 5 per-item rows
28	 * inside the "Cart-item-group" frame, i.e. genuinely SFCC-270/795's own per-item scope. It is
29	 * NOT the same as "Cart-level-messages" (a distinct sibling instance, 1186x52, that the same
30	 * top-level "WARNINGS SHOWN" frame (9323-90299) also contains at the page level) — that one is
31	 * SFCC-404's cart-level banner, a wholly different component this build does not touch. The two
32	 * share a parent frame and a similar 8px gap value, which is what makes them easy to conflate at
33	 * a glance; the "Cart Item"/"Cart-level-messages" instance names are what actually disambiguate
34	 * them, confirmed directly rather than inferred from proximity.
35	 *
36	 * So the single implicit node this recipe used to describe is no longer enough: `root` is now
37	 * the flex row wrapping the optional icon + the text, and `text` carries what used to be the
38	 * whole recipe's `baseStyle`.
39	 *
40	 * No separate `icon` part: `ZimmIcon`'s own `color` prop defaults to `currentColor`
41	 * (zimmIcon/index.tsx), and Chakra's `Icon` component passes `color` straight through as the
42	 * rendered SVG's own inline CSS `color` rather than resolving it to a token itself (confirmed
43	 * directly in `@chakra-ui/icon`'s `Icon` implementation) — so the icon element's own
44	 * `stroke="currentColor"` shapes (zimm.tsx's `InfoSolidIcon`) inherit `root`'s `color` via
45	 * ordinary CSS inheritance for free. Nothing to declare on this recipe's side for the icon.
46	 *
47	 * --- Typography: regular weight is a DELIBERATE override, on a DIFFERENT Figma node than the
48	 * one commit 5 (SFCC-270) corrected — read both before touching either ---
49	 * `textStyle: 'caption'` supplies the correct 12px size / 18px line-height pair, but this
50	 * codebase's `caption` textStyle (theme/foundation/typography.ts) is MEDIUM-weight
51	 * (`fontWeight: fontWeights.medium`) — that is exactly right for Figma's OTHER caption node,
52	 * `Default/Caption-strong` (the cart-item colour+size line — see
53	 * item-variant/item-variant.css.ts:73-84, which deliberately keeps `caption` with NO fontWeight
54	 * override for that reason, having removed an earlier, backwards override). THIS element is
55	 * Figma's plain, un-strong `Default/Caption` node, which is REGULAR-weight per the session-notes
56	 * citation above — the opposite correction, on a different string, elsewhere in the same design
57	 * file. `fontWeight` is therefore set explicitly below, on the `text` part, to override the
58	 * textStyle-expanded medium value back down to regular — the same "a direct CSS prop applied
59	 * after the textStyle expansion wins in Chakra's style pipeline" mechanism zimmButton.css.ts's
60	 * `sizes.lg`/`sizes.sm` already documents and relies on for the identical reason.
61	 *
62	 * `root.width: 'full'` reproduces Figma's own "w-full" annotation for this element explicitly,
63	 * rather than relying on this node's flex/stack parent to stretch it by default — moved here
64	 * from the (no-longer-existing) single node, since `root` is now the outer container.
65	 *
66	 * `root.alignItems: 'flex-start'`: top-aligned, not centred — the warning icon sits at the top
67	 * of what can be 2-line-wrapped text, not vertically centred against it. Confirmed via the
68	 * Figma metadata's own y-positions on the "Cart Item" instance cited above (9323:106685): the
69	 * icon instance sits at y=0 within its frame, the same top edge the text frame starts from.
70	 *
71	 * `root.gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)'` (8px): that same "Cart Item" instance places the 16px-wide icon at
72	 * x=0 and the text frame starting at x=24 — the 8px difference between them is the gap.
73	 *
74	 * Three variants, not two — corrected SFCC-795 plan step 3.3, 2026-09-18 (Marcel's direct Figma
75	 * inspector pull for the discount-label node). This paragraph used to read "the variants map
76	 * below only ever has the two keys `error`/`warning`; do not add a third," citing "SFCC-795
77	 * §11.2 build decisions" for that count. That citation does not hold up under a direct check:
78	 * `.claude/session-notes.md`'s actual "## 11.2 Cart Item" section (lines 710-740) never mentions
79	 * low-stock at all — checked directly, not assumed. The real, verifiable source for "no
80	 * low-stock messaging in the cart" is `.docs/prd/cart.md:70` (CAI-030): "Low-stock indicator
81	 * shown at size level — no quantity number displayed; not displayed in mini-cart or cart." That
82	 * prohibition is real and unchanged by this correction — a `LOW` size-level stock indicator has
83	 * no business rendering on a cart line regardless of how many variants this recipe has. What was
84	 * wrong was the COUNT, not the prohibition: `error`/`success`/`warning` are three real,
85	 * Figma-sourced cart-item-level treatments (this file's own docblock above cites each); a
86	 * fourth, low-stock-specific key is what remains forbidden.
87	 */
88	const baseStyle = {
89	  root: {
90	    display: 'flex',
91	    alignItems: 'flex-start',
92	    gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
93	    width: 'full',
94	  },
95	  text: {
96	    textStyle: 'caption',
97	    fontWeight: 'var(--zimm-font-weight-regular)',
98	    // Standard flexbox text-truncation-prevention: without these, a long message next to the
99	    // fixed-size icon in this flex row can be squeezed narrower than its own content instead of
100	    // wrapping onto its own available width. `flex: 1` lets the text claim the row's remaining
101	    // space (the icon, an intrinsically-sized SVG, takes only what it needs); `minWidth: 0`
102	    // overrides a flex item's own default `min-width: auto`, which would otherwise refuse to
103	    // shrink the text below its content's intrinsic width and push `root` wider than its own
104	    // `width: full`.
105	    flex: 1,
106	    minWidth: 0,
107	  },
108	};
109	
110	const variants = {
111	  // Figma `text/error` #9c0000 -> status.error (session-notes.md §11.10(6) colour audit).
112	  error: {
113	    root: {
114	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-status-error)',
115	    },
116	  },
117	  // Figma "Default/Caption" success text (cart-line discount label, "20% off applied") — pulled
118	  // directly by Marcel via Figma inspector, 2026-09-18: `color: var(--alias-color-text-success,
119	  // #2D5A3D)`. Byte-identical to this codebase's own status.success token: green[500] =
120	  // '#2d5a3d' (theme/foundation/colour.ts:27,80), registered as var(--zimm-color-status-success)
121	  // in zimmTokens.ts:73 — not a new token, the existing one. No icon on this variant, confirmed
122	  // directly with Marcel — same no-icon behaviour as `error` (see index.tsx's icon condition,
123	  // unchanged by this addition).
124	  success: {
125	    root: {
126	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-status-success)',
127	    },
128	  },
129	  // Figma `text/muted` / `text/subtlest` #969696 -> both collapse onto this one token, no
130	  // ambiguity in this codebase's own set (session-notes.md §11.10(6)). This is also the same
131	  // token the InfoSolidIcon's own real Figma export colour (#969696) coincidentally matches —
132	  // see that icon's own citation in zimm.tsx — not a second, independent confirmation of the
133	  // token choice, just a coincidence worth noting there and here.
134	  //
135	  // Max-quantity messaging ("Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size") uses THIS variant,
136	  // not `error` — even though its own requirement/AC text uses the word "error" to describe it.
137	  // That word is describing "user-facing feedback" in the requirement's own vocabulary, not
138	  // asserting the error SEVERITY tier: the actual Figma design and that story's own AC agree the
139	  // rendered treatment is grey/warning, not red/error. Deliberate word-vs-severity reconciliation,
140	  // settled at this build's planning gate — not a mistake, and not to be "corrected" back to
141	  // `error` by a future reader matching the word alone.
142	  warning: {
143	    root: {
144	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-muted)',
145	    },
146	  },
147	};
148	
149	export const ZimmInlineMessage = {
150	  parts: ['root', 'text'],
151	  baseStyle,
152	  variants,
153	};

15	import {FormattedMessage, useIntl} from 'react-intl'
16	import PropTypes from 'prop-types'

18	/**
19	 * This is the mobile implementation of the Chakra NumberInput. This simple component essentially
20	 * is a helper so we don't have to reuse the hooks every time we need a number input since design dictates
21	 * we use the moobile variation on all screens.
22	 *
23	 * NOTE: We can optionally put global logic we see if in here, and various styling decisions in this single
24	 * component.
25	 *
26	 * @param {*} props
27	 * @returns
28	 */
29	const QuantityPicker = (props) => {
30	    const intl = useIntl()
31	    const productName = props.productName
32	    const {getInputProps, getIncrementButtonProps, getDecrementButtonProps} = useNumberInput({
33	        ...props,
34	        // Defaults
35	        focusInputOnChange: false,
36	        onFocus: (e) => {
37	            // eslint-disable-next-line react/prop-types
38	            const {onFocus} = props
39	
40	            // This is useful for mobile devices, this allows the user to pop open the keyboard and set the
41	            // new quantity with one click.
42	            e.target.select()
43	
44	            // If there is a `onFocus` property define, call it with the event captured.
45	            // eslint-disable-next-line react/prop-types
46	            onFocus?.call(this, e)
47	        }
48	    })
49	
50	    const inc = getIncrementButtonProps({
51	        variant: 'outline',
52	        'aria-label': intl.formatMessage(
53	            {
54	                defaultMessage: 'Increment Quantity for {productName}',
55	                id: 'product_view.label.assistive_msg.quantity_increment'
56	            },
57	            {productName}
58	        )
59	    })
60	    const dec = getDecrementButtonProps({
61	        variant: 'outline',
62	        'aria-label': intl.formatMessage(
63	            {
64	                defaultMessage: 'Decrement Quantity for {productName}',
65	                id: 'product_view.label.assistive_msg.quantity_decrement'
66	            },
67	            {productName}
68	        )
69	    })
70	    const input = getInputProps({
71	        maxWidth: '44px',
72	        textAlign: 'center',
73	        'aria-label': intl.formatMessage({
74	            defaultMessage: 'Quantity',
75	            id: 'product_view.label.quantity'
76	        })
77	    })
78	
79	    // Accessibility improvements:
80	    // 1. Allow keyboard focus on the buttons - Chakra overrides values passed to get*ButtonProps()
81	    inc.tabIndex = ''
82	    dec.tabIndex = ''
83	    // 2. Allow Space or Enter key to trigger buttons
84	    // Hitting space/enter triggers a "click" event, but the component listens for "mousedown".
85	    // We can't reuse the buttons' onMouseDown handler, so instead we hijack the input's onKeyDown.
86	    // @ref https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui/blob/%40chakra-ui/react%402.7.0/packages/components/number-input/src/use-number-input.ts#L333-L334
87	    inc.onKeyDown = (evt) => {
88	        if (evt.key === ' ' || evt.key === 'Enter') {
89	            evt.key = 'ArrowUp'
90	            input.onKeyDown(evt)
91	        }
92	    }
93	    dec.onKeyDown = (evt) => {
94	        if (evt.key === ' ' || evt.key === 'Enter') {
95	            evt.key = 'ArrowDown'
96	            input.onKeyDown(evt)
97	        }
98	    }
99	
100	    return (
101	        <HStack>
102	            <Button data-testid="quantity-decrement" {...dec}>
103	                <FormattedMessage
104	                    id="product_view.label.quantity_decrement"
105	                    defaultMessage={'\u2212'} // HTML −
106	                />
107	            </Button>
108	            <Input {...input} />
109	            <Button data-testid="quantity-increment" {...inc}>
110	                <FormattedMessage id="product_view.label.quantity_increment" defaultMessage="+" />
111	            </Button>
112	        </HStack>
113	    )
114	}
115	
116	QuantityPicker.propTypes = {
117	    productName: PropTypes.string
118	}
119	
120	export default QuantityPicker

15	 * Recipe — cart-line quantity stepper (SFCC-271). Two `ZimmButton variant="icon"` controls sit
16	 * either side of a numeric value display; all hover/press/focus/disabled states for the buttons
17	 * themselves live entirely in zimmButton.css.ts (untouched by this file — see index.tsx, which
18	 * composes ZimmButton rather than restyling it).

21	 * `0.5rem`/8px exactly, so this needs no new token). Deliberate, disclosed departure from

28	 * button boxes therefore reproduces the ~12px glyph-to-glyph spacing Figma's raw annotation
29	 * intended (6px inset + 8px gap + 6px inset from centre-of-glyph to centre-of-glyph ≈ the

31	 * alternative (an 8px gap measured glyph-edge to glyph-edge with no inset accounted for) would
32	 * under-space them relative to Figma; this recipe's 8px is the touch-target-aware equivalent,

36	 * in this build step; `body2Strong` (14px / 500 weight / 18px line-height, typography.ts) is the
37	 * nearest existing textStyle — PROVISIONAL pending UI-designer confirmation, same disclosure
38	 * pattern as zimmSizeSelector.css.ts's own oneSize label. Dims to OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED when
39	 * `disabled` (the whole control is OOS/unavailable, not just one bound) — sourced from
40	 * zimmCartItemShared.ts rather than restated here or imported from zimmButton.css.ts, so the
41	 * value display and the two buttons beside it (which get their own dimming entirely from
42	 * zimmButton.css.ts's `icon` variant, once the caller passes `ariaDisabled` through — nothing
43	 * about that is duplicated here) can never visually drift apart, without this recipe reaching
44	 * into an unrelated atom's styling module for the number. Applying the SAME opacity to `root`
45	 * as well would double it up on the buttons (0.4 × 0.4 = 0.16, not 0.4) — deliberately scoped to
46	 * `value` only for that reason.
47	 */
48	export const ZimmQuantityStepper = {
49	  parts: ['root', 'value'],
50	  baseStyle: ({ disabled }: ZimmQuantityStepperStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
51	    root: {
52	      display: 'inline-flex',
53	      alignItems: 'center',
54	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
55	    },
56	    value: {
57	      display: 'inline-flex',
58	      alignItems: 'center',
59	      justifyContent: 'center',
60	      textStyle: 'body2Strong',
61	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
62	      opacity: disabled ? OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED : 1,
63	    },
64	  }),

import { OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED } from 'app/components/ui-kits/zimmCartItemShared';

/** State the component feeds in so the recipe can resolve the value display's dimmed state.
 *  Named `disabled` (not e.g. `isUnavailable`) to match the resolution-prop convention already
 *  used by every other function-form baseStyle in this codebase (zimmTextInput.css.ts's own
 *  `disabled` key) — `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s PROP_COMBINATIONS harness only
 *  exercises the fixed key set `{inverse, disabled, hasError, focused, filled}`, so a
 *  differently-named boolean here would never have its `true` branch walked by that guard. */
export type ZimmQuantityStepperStyleProps = {
  disabled?: boolean;
};

/**
 * Recipe — cart-line quantity stepper (SFCC-271). Two `ZimmButton variant="icon"` controls sit
 * either side of a numeric value display; all hover/press/focus/disabled states for the buttons
 * themselves live entirely in zimmButton.css.ts (untouched by this file — see index.tsx, which
 * composes ZimmButton rather than restyling it).
 *
 * `root` — the flex row. Gap is 8px (`var(--zimm-scale-xs)` — foundation/spacing.ts's `xs` is
 * `0.5rem`/8px exactly, so this needs no new token). Deliberate, disclosed departure from
 * Figma's own raw annotation, which shows a 12px gap around a bare 12px glyph with no drawn
 * touch target at all. ZimmButton's `icon` size variant already resolves both buttons to a 24px
 * touch target (zimmButton.css.ts `sizes.icon` — `minW`/`minH`: `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`, cited
 * there against WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8, and matching the Figma node's own literal name
 * `touchTarget` at value 24) — i.e. 6px of invisible padding is already added on every side of
 * each 12px glyph before this gap is even applied. An 8px authored gap between the two 24px
 * button boxes therefore reproduces the ~12px glyph-to-glyph spacing Figma's raw annotation
 * intended (6px inset + 8px gap + 6px inset from centre-of-glyph to centre-of-glyph ≈ the
 * annotated 12px), without shrinking either button below its accessible 24px target — the
 * alternative (an 8px gap measured glyph-edge to glyph-edge with no inset accounted for) would
 * under-space them relative to Figma; this recipe's 8px is the touch-target-aware equivalent,
 * not a straight copy of the raw annotation.
 *
 * `value` — the numeric display. No Figma node or type-style was supplied for this specific text
 * in this build step; `body2Strong` (14px / 500 weight / 18px line-height, typography.ts) is the
 * nearest existing textStyle — PROVISIONAL pending UI-designer confirmation, same disclosure
 * pattern as zimmSizeSelector.css.ts's own oneSize label. Dims to OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED when
 * `disabled` (the whole control is OOS/unavailable, not just one bound) — sourced from
 * zimmCartItemShared.ts rather than restated here or imported from zimmButton.css.ts, so the
 * value display and the two buttons beside it (which get their own dimming entirely from
 * zimmButton.css.ts's `icon` variant, once the caller passes `ariaDisabled` through — nothing
 * about that is duplicated here) can never visually drift apart, without this recipe reaching

import type { ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';

/**
 * `c_maxOrderQuantity` is a Zimmermann-custom SFCC attribute — a real BM site preference
 * (Integer, default 3, min 1, per-site) surfaced onto the SCAPI product response via a
 * `dw.ocapi.shop.product.afterGET` hook, per Confluence `TSD-SFCC-268` (406913046). It has no
 * typed field on the base SDK's `Product` type — it only reaches this shape via that type's own
 * `{[key: string]: any}` index signature, the same situation
 * `overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts` lines 16-23 document for a
 * different custom attribute (`c_productBadges`). Narrowed here to a local type rather than
 * trusting `any` at the call site, per AGENTS.md's Gotchas: "Commerce SDK types not importable
 * ... declare a narrow local type."
 *
 * Typed `unknown`, not `number | undefined`: this function's whole job is validating a value
 * that may legitimately arrive absent, as `0`, negative, or non-numeric (see the pass criteria
 * this file's own test covers) — typing it as `number | undefined` would assert a guarantee the
 * real BM data doesn't have.
 *
 * As of this commit `TSD-SFCC-268` is still `v0.1 Draft` (Technical Lead sign-off Pending) and a
 * live dev-sandbox probe found no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product — the `afterGET` hook is
 * not deployed yet. Reading the field with the fallback below degrades to today's hardcoded
 * behaviour while that remains true, and picks up the real per-site value the day the hook ships,
 * with no further frontend change needed.
 */
type ProductWithMaxOrderQuantity = ShopperProductsTypes.Product & {
  c_maxOrderQuantity?: unknown;
};

/**
 * Frontend fallback when no valid `c_maxOrderQuantity` is present. Matches
 * `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`'s own `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY` value (3) exactly
 * (see that file's lines 124-125: "Frontend-enforced limit (SFCC-196). SFCC has no platform
 * max-order-quantity field."), but is deliberately its own, independent constant rather than a
 * shared/promoted one — the TSD's resolution order is product override (SFCC-703) -> site
 * preference -> this hardcoded value, so a constant shared between the PDP and this cart-facing
 * util would need reworking the day the real per-site preference ships anyway.
 */
const DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY = 3;

/**
 * Reads the real per-product order-quantity cap off a SCAPI product response
 * (`c_maxOrderQuantity`), falling back to `DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY` when the attribute is
 * absent or not a valid, usable cap (zero, negative, or non-numeric) — see this file's own
 * module docblock for why a shared constant is deliberately not used here.
 *
 * @param product A SCAPI product response (or product-shaped object) that may carry
 * `c_maxOrderQuantity`.
 * @returns The product's real max order quantity, or `DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY` (3) when no
 * valid value is present.
 */
export const getMaxOrderQuantity = (product: ProductWithMaxOrderQuantity): number => {
  const value = product?.c_maxOrderQuantity;
  return typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value) && value > 0 ? value : DEFAULT_MAX_ORDER_QUANTITY;
};

16	  onClose: () => void;
17	  /** Number of line items in the bag. Drives the header title ("BAG • {itemCount}" vs
18	   *  "YOUR BAG IS EMPTY") and whether `children` or the interim empty-state placeholder renders. */
19	  itemCount: number;
20	  /** Element to focus once the drawer finishes closing — see ZimmDrawer's own doc (AC10
21	   *  focus-return); without this Chakra falls back to focusing document.body. */
22	  finalFocusRef?: React.RefObject<HTMLElement>;
23	  /** Cart line items. This organism owns no item-rendering logic itself — the caller supplies
24	   *  the list (SFCC-270's ProductItem, wired in a later commit in this same plan). Rendered only
25	   *  while itemCount > 0. */
26	  children: React.ReactNode;
27	  /** Reserved slot for SFCC-404's message-aggregation system (validation/error/promo banners).
28	   *  Always rendered, even with nothing passed — see zimmCartDrawer.css.ts's `messages` part:
29	   *  the band reserves height regardless, so the drawer doesn't change position when a message
30	   *  appears or disappears. */
31	  messages?: React.ReactNode;
32	  /** Reserved slot for SFCC-275's button group (checkout / continue shopping). Not built in this
33	   *  commit (SFCC-315 is shell-only) — this organism only provides the slot it will render into
34	   *  later. */
35	  footer?: React.ReactNode;
36	};
37	
38	/**
39	 * SFCC-315 — the Cart drawer shell. Wraps ZimmDrawer (size="xLarge") with the cart-specific
40	 * header title, a height-reserving messages band, a responsive items/totals layout, and a
41	 * footer slot.
42	 *
43	 * Deliberately not wired to a trigger yet — no `_app`/`product-view` changes, no
44	 * `useCartDrawer` hook, no button-group content, no real empty-state body, no message
45	 * aggregation. All of those are separate, later commits in this same 18-commit plan — this
46	 * organism is exercised only via its own Storybook stories today.
47	 *
48	 * @param props see ZimmCartDrawerProps
49	 */
50	export const ZimmCartDrawer = ({
51	  isOpen,
52	  onClose,
53	  itemCount,
54	  finalFocusRef,
55	  children,
56	  messages,
57	  footer,
58	}: ZimmCartDrawerProps) => {
59	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_DRAWER_RECIPE, {});
60	  const title = itemCount === 0 ? 'YOUR BAG IS EMPTY' : `BAG • ${itemCount}`;
61	
62	  return (
63	    <ZimmDrawer isOpen={isOpen} onClose={onClose} size="xLarge" title={title} finalFocusRef={finalFocusRef}>
64	      <chakra.div __css={styles.messages}>{messages}</chakra.div>
65	      <chakra.div __css={styles.body}>
66	        {itemCount === 0 ? <chakra.p textStyle="body2">{EMPTY_BAG_PLACEHOLDER_TEXT}</chakra.p> : children}
67	      </chakra.div>
68	      <chakra.div __css={styles.footer}>{footer}</chakra.div>
69	    </ZimmDrawer>
70	  );
71	};

2	import { DRAWER_HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT } from 'app/theme/components/zimmDrawerShared';
3	
4	// Figma's actual named drawer sizes (SFCC-898) — five named sizes, not the three/four this
5	// file previously guessed at. Each name below matches Figma's own naming exactly, so there's
6	// no re-deriving which number belongs to which concept next time this file is touched:
7	//
8	//   Desktop Large — 50%  — Product Details, Filters (desktop width)
9	//   Tablet        — 80%  — Product Details, Filters (tablet width)
10	//   Desktop Small — 25%  — Notify Me, Wishlist, Find in Boutique, Regional Storefront,
11	//                           Cookies, Login
12	//   X-Large       — 82%  — Cart. SFCC-11: this is the named-size *library* annotation, not a
13	//                           measurement of the real Cart composition — see `WIDTH_XLARGE` below,
14	//                           which corrects it a second time against the actual frames.
15	//   Mobile        — unchanged, the baseStyle treatment every variant collapses to below `md`.
16	//
17	// An earlier revision of this file measured 82% off a Figma frame annotated "Tablet = 82% of
18	// screen" and used it as `small`'s (now `tablet`'s) value — that frame's annotation was wrong
19	// (or superseded): 82% is actually X-Large's value (Cart), a completely different drawer this
20	// codebase hasn't built yet, and Tablet is genuinely 80%. Corrected once confirmed directly
21	// against the list above, not another single frame's own label.
22	const WIDTH_LARGE = '50%';
23	const WIDTH_TABLET = '80%';
24	// The original width set when this drawer shell was first built (2026-08-27) — matches Figma's
25	// "Desktop Small" exactly. Used by every viewport-independent narrow utility drawer (Find in
26	// Boutique today; Notify Me/Wishlist/Regional Storefront/Cookies/Login once those exist).
27	const WIDTH_SMALL = '25%';
28	// SFCC-11 (Cart build): the "X-Large — 82%" library annotation two paragraphs up is the
29	// named-size *system* value, not a measurement of the actual Cart composition. Re-measured the
30	// real frames directly (node 9323:65888 at 1920px, node 9323:65895 at 1440px, file
31	// QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs) — the cart panel itself (frame "pdp/drawer") is a FIXED 1186px at
32	// both widths; the backdrop gap grows instead of the panel. 82% of 1920 is 1574px — 388px
33	// wider than designed. This is the same annotation-vs-measurement trap the comment above
34	// already records once for Tablet; it recurred here for X-Large. 74.125rem = 1186px.
35	// Widths/min-widths/max-widths across drawer sizes are a live, unsettled area as of
36	// 2026-09-17 (Marcel) — this ships to the current measured Figma spec and may be
37	// reconciled once that broader call is made; not a final word on the sizing model.
38	// audit-allow: Figma-confirmed fixed width with no --zimm-scale equivalent at this value.
39	const WIDTH_XLARGE = '74.125rem'; // 1186px
40	
41	// PDP drawer leaves a strip of backdrop visible below the panel on mobile (SFCC-736 AC 9,
42	// PO-approved 2026-08-21 — "so a user can easily navigate out"). Re-measured against node
43	// 40002218:42903 (SFCC-898): overlay 956px tall, panel 898px tall — exactly 58px. Only the
44	// `mobileGap` variant opts into this; the baseStyle defaults to full-height so utility
45	// drawers (wishlist auth, etc.) don't need to explicitly override it. No named spacing scale
46	// step lands on 58px — provisional raw value pending a foundation token.
47	const MOBILE_BOTTOM_GAP = '3.625rem'; // 58px
48	
49	// Close-button inset, measured from the pdp/drawer header frames. `tablet`/`small`/`xLarge`/
50	// `mobile` all share the same measured inset (32px/40px) at every width — only `large` switches
51	// to the wider 48px/64px inset, at/above the tablet breakpoint. Below that breakpoint `large`'s
52	// own override doesn't apply either, and the baseStyle inset is used instead, which is also how
53	// the whole drawer collapses to the mobile treatment on a narrow viewport regardless of `size`.
54	const INSET_COMPACT = { top: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)', right: 'var(--zimm-scale-2xl)' };
55	const INSET_LARGE = { top: 'var(--zimm-scale-1200)', right: 'var(--zimm-scale-4xl)' };
56	
57	// Header constants — from Figma drawer/header frame measurements.
58	// Compact horizontal inset (small/mobile): px=32px. Large desktop: px=64px.
59	// Small desktop header uses py=24px. Large desktop: container height=120px (row centred).
60	// Mobile base: container height=72px.
61	const HEADER_PADDING_COMPACT_X = 'var(--zimm-scale-2xl)'; // 32px
62	const HEADER_PADDING_LARGE_X = 'var(--zimm-scale-4xl)'; // 64px
63	const HEADER_PADDING_Y = 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'; // 24px — small desktop py
64	// audit-allow: Figma-confirmed container heights with no --zimm-scale equivalents at these values.
65	const HEADER_HEIGHT_LARGE = '120px';
66	const HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE = '72px';
67	
68	export const ZimmDrawer = {
69	  parts: ['overlay', 'content', 'closeButton', 'header', 'headerTitle'],
70	  baseStyle: {
71	    // Explicit position/inset rather than relying on Chakra's own built-in `Drawer` overlay
72	    // styling — confirmed via inspection that it doesn't apply (renders `position: static`,
73	    // zero size) when the `<Drawer>` isn't given Chakra's own `size` prop, which this component
74	    // deliberately omits (see maxWidth note below). Owning it here avoids depending on that.
75	    overlay: {
76	      position: 'fixed',
77	      inset: 0,
78	      background: 'var(--zimm-color-opacity-50)',
79	      zIndex: 'overlay',
80	    },
81	    content: {
82	      // Chakra's own <DrawerContent> baked in a default white background
83	      // (@chakra-ui/theme's modal.js `baseStyleDialog`: `bg: colors.white`) that this recipe
84	      // never needed to set itself while that component was still in use — now that
85	      // ZimmDrawer hand-rolls its own content element (see index.tsx's file-level comment),
86	      // nothing supplies one unless it's set here. Matches Figma's pdp/drawer panel background
87	      // (bg-[var(--brand/color/palette/white,white)]) — --zimm-color-bg-07 resolves to the
88	      // same grey.white value (SFCC-898 — the panel briefly had no background at all).
89	      background: 'var(--zimm-color-bg-07)',
90	      width: '100%',
91	      // Matches `width` at every step below — Chakra's own `Drawer` theme defaults to
92	      // `size="xs"` (maxW 20rem) when no `size` prop is passed to `<Drawer>` (deliberate: its
93	      // fixed size scale has no 50%/25% steps), and that default `maxW` otherwise still caps
94	      // our own `width` override since we never reset it.
95	      maxWidth: '100%',
96	      // A `height` reduction, not a `bottom` offset — Chakra's own Slide transition (see
97	      // @chakra-ui/transition's slide.js `placement: 'right'` case) pins the sliding wrapper
98	      // with `position: fixed; top: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0`, a definite height. `bottom` on
99	      // this `position: relative` DrawerContent just shifts the box within that instead of
100	      // reliably opening a gap (SFCC-898 — mobile bottom gap wasn't rendering at all); a
101	      // percentage `height` resolves cleanly against that definite-height ancestor instead.
102	      // CodeRabbit (PR review): baseStyle should default to full-height so utility drawers
103	      // don't inherit the PDP-specific 58px backdrop strip — moved to the `mobile` variant.
104	      height: '100%',
105	      // Header stays fixed; only the content area (ZimmPdpDrawer's own `content` part) scrolls —
106	      // AC 10, "content area scrolls independently without the tab header scrolling".
107	      display: 'flex',
108	      flexDirection: 'column',
109	      overflow: 'hidden',
110	    },
111	    // Was missing `position: absolute` since this component's original commit — the
112	    // top/right insets below were silently no-ops (closeButton rendered as a normal in-flow
113	    // block instead of overlaying the header's corner), which is the root cause of SFCC-898's
114	    // close-button-misaligned-with-tabs defect across every breakpoint.
115	    //
116	    // height/display/alignItems/justifyContent: matches zimmTabs.css.ts's `menu.minHeight`
117	    // (DRAWER_HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT, zimmDrawerShared.ts) and centers the icon inside it — the
118	    // close icon's own intrinsic size doesn't equal the tab row's real rendered height, so
119	    // matching only `top` between the two (as before) left their vertical centers slightly
120	    // offset (SFCC-898, mobile). Only applies to the floating close button (no `title` passed) —
121	    // the inline title-row close button below is a normal flex child, not absolutely positioned.
122	    closeButton: {
123	      position: 'absolute',
124	      ...INSET_COMPACT,
125	      height: DRAWER_HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT,
126	      display: 'flex',
127	      alignItems: 'center',
128	      justifyContent: 'center',
129	    },
130	    // Drawer header — title (flex-1, left) + close button (right).
131	    // baseStyle applies the mobile/compact treatment: px=32px, container h=72px centred.
132	    // SFCC-926 (Figma): paddingBlock is 0 at mobile so the 72px minHeight controls the height
133	    // (flex centering handles vertical alignment). At md+ 24px block padding applies — matching
134	    // Figma's "small desktop py" spec without overriding the mobile 72px container height.
135	    header: {
136	      display: 'flex',
137	      alignItems: 'center',
138	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
139	      backgroundColor: 'var(--zimm-color-text-inverse)',
140	      paddingInline: HEADER_PADDING_COMPACT_X,
141	      paddingBlock: 0,
142	      minHeight: HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE,
143	      flexShrink: 0,
144	      [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
145	        paddingBlock: HEADER_PADDING_Y,
146	      },
147	    },
148	    headerTitle: {
149	      display: 'flex',
150	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)',
151	      alignItems: 'center',
152	      flex: '1 0 0',
153	      minWidth: 0,
154	      overflow: 'hidden',
155	      whiteSpace: 'nowrap',
156	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
157	    },
158	  },
159	  variants: {
160	    large: {
161	      content: {
162	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
163	          width: WIDTH_LARGE,
164	          maxWidth: WIDTH_LARGE,
165	          height: '100%',
166	        },
167	      },
168	      closeButton: {
169	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: INSET_LARGE,
170	      },
171	      header: {
172	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
173	          paddingInline: HEADER_PADDING_LARGE_X,
174	          minHeight: HEADER_HEIGHT_LARGE,
175	        },
176	      },
177	    },
178	    // Figma's "Tablet" size — the tablet-range step for Product Details/Filters, which
179	    // graduates to `large` (Desktop Large) at the desktop breakpoint via the caller's own
180	    // useBreakpointValue (ZimmPdpDrawer never selects this variant itself).
181	    tablet: {
182	      content: {
183	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
184	          width: WIDTH_TABLET,
185	          maxWidth: WIDTH_TABLET,
186	          height: '100%',
187	        },
188	      },
189	    },
190	    // Figma's "Desktop Small" — always narrow, at every width above the mobile collapse. No
191	    // js-level graduation to another variant the way `tablet` graduates to `large` — this is
192	    // the whole point for its utility-drawer consumers (Find in Boutique today).
193	    small: {
194	      content: {
195	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
196	          width: WIDTH_SMALL,
197	          maxWidth: WIDTH_SMALL,
198	          height: '100%',
199	        },
200	      },
201	    },
202	    // Figma's "X-Large" (Cart) — not consumed anywhere yet (Cart is a full page today, not a
203	    // drawer), but the real value is already here under the right name for when that changes.
204	    // `maxWidth: '100%'` (not WIDTH_XLARGE) so a viewport narrower than 1186px but still ≥ `md`
205	    // doesn't overflow.
206	    xLarge: {
207	      content: {
208	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
209	          width: WIDTH_XLARGE,
210	          maxWidth: '100%',
211	          height: '100%',
212	        },
213	      },
214	      header: {
215	        [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
216	          minHeight: 'unset',
217	          paddingBlock: HEADER_PADDING_Y,
218	        },
219	      },
220	    },
221	    // CodeRabbit (PR review): 58px backdrop strip is PDP-specific (SFCC-736 AC 9, PO-approved)
222	    // and must not apply to utility drawers — scoped here to the explicit `mobile` variant.
223	    // Figma's "Mobile" size — only drawers that need the strip opt in; utility drawers
224	    // (wishlist auth, etc.) use `large` instead, which collapses to full-height via baseStyle.
225	    mobile: {
226	      content: {
227	        height: `calc(100% - ${MOBILE_BOTTOM_GAP})`,
228	      },
229	    },
230	  },

1	// Shared between the drawer/tabs recipe files that must stay in the same 44px band —
2	// zimmDrawer.css.ts's `closeButton` and zimmTabs.css.ts's `menu` — so the value can't drift the
3	// way a copy-pasted literal would. Not a general-purpose theme module — scope stays this one
4	// drawer-header row; see .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md's co-location guidance for the pattern
5	// this follows (footerShared.ts is the reference example).
6	
7	// Figma's drawer-header-options row height (SFCC-898) — measured at 44px on every captured
8	// frame (desktop, tablet, mobile). ZimmDrawer's closeButton is a separate, independently
9	// positioned element from ZimmTabs' own tab row (not a child of the same flex row the way
10	// Figma has them), so matching this same explicit height on both is what keeps their vertical
11	// centers aligned by construction rather than by coincidence of the tab text's own line-height.
12	export const DRAWER_HEADER_ROW_HEIGHT = '2.75rem'; // 44px
13

1	// Spacing scale — source of truth: Figma node 2081:52901 (Design-Workspace > Spacing)
2	// Added to theme.space via extendTheme — Chakra's numeric defaults are preserved.
3	// Values are in rem so spacing scales with a user's root font-size / browser zoom
4	// (WCAG 1.4.4). Border widths (below) intentionally stay in px: hairline geometry
5	// shouldn't scale with zoom.
6	
7	// prettier-ignore
8	export const spacing = {
9	  '3xs': '0.125rem', // 2px
10	  '2xs': '0.25rem',  // 4px
11	  xs:    '0.5rem',   // 8px
12	  s:     '0.75rem',  // 12px
13	  m:     '1rem',     // 16px
14	  l:     '1.25rem',  // 20px
15	  xl:    '1.5rem',   // 24px
16	  '2xl': '2rem',     // 32px
17	  '3xl': '2.5rem',   // 40px
18	  '4xl': '4rem',     // 64px
19	  '5xl': '5rem',     // 80px
20	  '6xl': '8rem',     // 128px
21	  '7xl': '10rem',    // 160px
22	} as const;
23	
24	// Border widths — source of truth: Handover tokens/spacing.css (--zimm-border-width-default).
25	// Registered as theme.borderWidths; the CSS-var twin already exists in zimmTokens.ts.
26	export const borderWidths = {
27	  default: '1px',
28	} as const;
29	
30	// Focus-ring outline offsets — hairline geometry, stays px like border widths above.
31	// `secondary` clears the 1px border on the secondary button variant (Handover
32	// button.md §focus) — the name describes that variant, not a generic scale step,
33	// since nothing else currently needs a third offset value.
34	export const focusRingOffsets = {
35	  default: '2px',
36	  secondary: '3px',
37	} as const;
38

1	// Icon sizes — source: Zimmermann Design System 2026 (Handover tokens.md § Icon Sizes)
2	//
3	// Deliberately NOT registered as `theme.sizes`. Chakra's `sizes.lg` is 32rem and
4	// backs every `w`/`h`/`boxSize` token across the base retail-react-app, so
5	// remapping these names would resize base components. Import these constants
6	// directly instead — the same pattern component overrides already use for
7	// FONT_MEDIUM: `<Icon boxSize={iconSizes.lg} />`.
8	export const iconSizes = {
9	  xl: '24px',
10	  lg: '20px',
11	  md: '16px',
12	  sm: '12px',
13	} as const;
14	
15	// Action (button) sizing — source: Handover tokens/spacing.css (--zimm-size-action-*).
16	// The CSS-var twins already exist in zimmTokens.ts. zimmButton.css.ts (the single source
17	// of truth for actual button styling) uses var(--zimm-size-action-height-lg/md) directly,
18	// which resolves to these Figma-confirmed values (52px / 40px).
19	export const actionSizes = {
20	  height: {
21	    lg: '52px',
22	    md: '40px',
23	  },
24	  paddingX: {
25	    lg: '32px',
26	    md: '20px',
27	  },
28	  gap: '16px',
29	} as const;
30	
31	// Mega-menu sizing — source: Zimmermann Design System 2026, Figma node 40002429:7215
32	// (two-column "Expanded Menu" Nav Group, confirmed against SFCC-883).
33	export const megaMenuSizes = {
34	  twoColumnMaxWidth: '700px',
35	} as const;
36

1	// CSS custom property registry — source: Zimmermann Design System 2026
2	// All --zimm-* variables, derived from the other foundation/* files (the actual source
3	// of truth, ported from the Figma-to-React work) rather than retyped here. Injected onto
4	// :root by _app-config/index.tsx via <Global> from @emotion/react, so the .zimm-* classes
5	// in globalStyles.ts can resolve their var(--zimm-*) references.
6	import { FONT_MEDIUM, FONT_REGULAR, FONT_SERIF } from './fonts';
7	import { colors } from './colour';
8	import { fontSizes, lineHeights, letterSpacings, fontWeights } from './typography';
9	import { spacing, borderWidths, focusRingOffsets } from './spacing';
10	import { iconSizes, actionSizes, megaMenuSizes } from './sizes';
11	import { grid } from './gridSystem';
12	import { motion } from './motion';
13	
14	export const zimmTokens: Record<string, string> = {
15	  // ---- Brand / Primitive: Greys ----
16	  '--zimm-color-grey-black': colors.grey.black,

// CSS custom property registry — source: Zimmermann Design System 2026
// All --zimm-* variables, derived from the other foundation/* files (the actual source
// of truth, ported from the Figma-to-React work) rather than retyped here. Injected onto
// :root by _app-config/index.tsx via <Global> from @emotion/react, so the .zimm-* classes
// in globalStyles.ts can resolve their var(--zimm-*) references.
import { FONT_MEDIUM, FONT_REGULAR, FONT_SERIF } from './fonts';
import { colors } from './colour';
import { fontSizes, lineHeights, letterSpacings, fontWeights } from './typography';
import { spacing, borderWidths, focusRingOffsets } from './spacing';
import { iconSizes, actionSizes, megaMenuSizes } from './sizes';
import { grid } from './gridSystem';
import { motion } from './motion';

export const zimmTokens: Record<string, string> = {
  // ---- Brand / Primitive: Greys ----
  '--zimm-color-grey-black': colors.grey.black,
  '--zimm-color-grey-900': colors.grey[900],
  '--zimm-color-grey-800': colors.grey[800],
  '--zimm-color-grey-700': colors.grey[700],

  '--zimm-color-grey-100': colors.grey[100],
  '--zimm-color-grey-white': colors.grey.white,

  // ---- Brand / Primitive: Ivory ----
  '--zimm-color-ivory-400': colors.ivory[400],
  '--zimm-color-ivory-300': colors.ivory[300],
  '--zimm-color-ivory-200': colors.ivory[200],
  '--zimm-color-ivory-100': colors.ivory[100],

  // ---- Brand / Primitive: Status ----
  '--zimm-color-coral-500': colors.coral[500],
  '--zimm-color-green-500': colors.green[500],
  '--zimm-color-orange-500': colors.orange[500],
  '--zimm-color-red-500': colors.red[500],

  // ---- Brand / Primitive: Opacity (base: grey/900) ----
  '--zimm-color-opacity-50': colors.opacity[50],
  '--zimm-color-opacity-40': colors.opacity[40],
  '--zimm-color-opacity-30': colors.opacity[30],
  '--zimm-color-opacity-15': colors.opacity[15],

  // ---- Alias / Semantic: Text ----
  '--zimm-color-text-default': colors.text.default,
  '--zimm-color-text-inverse': colors.text.inverse,
  '--zimm-color-text-inverse-grey': colors.text.inverseGrey,
  '--zimm-color-text-secondary': colors.text.secondary,
  '--zimm-color-text-muted': colors.text.muted,

  // ---- Alias / Semantic: Background ----
  '--zimm-color-bg-01': colors.background['01'],

  '--zimm-color-bg-03': colors.background['03'],
  '--zimm-color-bg-04': colors.background['04'],
  '--zimm-color-bg-05': colors.background['05'],
  '--zimm-color-bg-06': colors.background['06'],
  '--zimm-color-bg-07': colors.background['07'],

  // ---- Alias / Semantic: Border ----
  '--zimm-color-border-default': colors.border.default,
  '--zimm-color-border-secondary': colors.border.secondary,
  '--zimm-color-border-focus': colors.border.focus,
  '--zimm-color-border-forms': colors.border.forms,

  // ---- Composite: Focus ring ----
  '--zimm-focus-ring': `${borderWidths.default} solid ${colors.border.focus}`,
  '--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default': focusRingOffsets.default,

  // ---- Alias / Semantic: Status ----
  '--zimm-color-status-success': colors.status.success,

  // ---- Alias / Semantic: Action: Primary ----
  '--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-default': colors.action.primary.bgDefault,
  '--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-hover': colors.action.primary.bgHover,
  '--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-pressed': colors.action.primary.bgPressed,

  '--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-focused': colors.action.primary.bgFocused,
  '--zimm-color-action-primary-text': colors.action.primary.text,
  '--zimm-color-action-primary-text-disabled': colors.action.primary.textDisabled,

  // ---- Alias / Semantic: Action: Secondary ----
  '--zimm-color-action-secondary-border': colors.action.secondary.border,
  '--zimm-color-action-secondary-bg-hover': colors.action.secondary.bgHover,
  '--zimm-color-action-secondary-text': colors.action.secondary.text,
  '--zimm-color-action-secondary-text-inverse': colors.action.secondary.textInverse,
  '--zimm-color-action-secondary-text-disabled': colors.action.secondary.textDisabled,

  // ---- Typography: Font families ----
  // Both heading and body resolve to the same stack, headed by Futura Round.
  // Sourced from ./fonts so the CSS-variable surface and theme.fonts cannot drift
  // apart: text styled by a .zimm-* class and text styled by a Chakra prop must
  // fall back to the same face when Futura Round is unavailable. This intentionally
  // carries the richer fallback stack rather than the Handover's bare

  '--zimm-font-family-heading': FONT_MEDIUM,
  '--zimm-font-family-body': FONT_REGULAR,

  // ---- Typography: Font sizes ----

  '--zimm-font-size-xs': fontSizes.xs,
  '--zimm-font-size-2xs': fontSizes['2xs'],

  '--zimm-font-size-4xs': fontSizes['4xs'],

  // ---- Typography: Line heights ----
  '--zimm-font-lineheight-md': lineHeights.md,
  '--zimm-font-lineheight-xs': lineHeights.xs,
  '--zimm-font-lineheight-2xs': lineHeights['2xs'],
  '--zimm-font-lineheight-3xs': lineHeights['3xs'],
  '--zimm-font-lineheight-4xs': lineHeights['4xs'],

  // ---- Typography: Letter spacing ----
  '--zimm-font-letterspacing-sm': letterSpacings.sm,
  '--zimm-font-letterspacing-xs': letterSpacings.xs,
  '--zimm-font-letterspacing-2xs': letterSpacings['2xs'], // -0.14px — see typography.ts
  '--zimm-font-letterspacing-footer': letterSpacings.footer,

  // ---- Typography: Font weights ----
  '--zimm-font-weight-medium': fontWeights.medium,
  '--zimm-font-weight-regular': fontWeights.regular,

  // ---- Spacing scale (named) ----
  '--zimm-scale-3xs': spacing['3xs'],
  '--zimm-scale-2xs': spacing['2xs'],
  '--zimm-scale-xs': spacing.xs,
  '--zimm-scale-s': spacing.s,
  '--zimm-scale-m': spacing.m,
  '--zimm-scale-l': spacing.l,
  '--zimm-scale-xl': spacing.xl,
  '--zimm-scale-2xl': spacing['2xl'],
  '--zimm-scale-3xl': spacing['3xl'],
  '--zimm-scale-4xl': spacing['4xl'],
  '--zimm-scale-5xl': spacing['5xl'],
  '--zimm-scale-6xl': spacing['6xl'],
  '--zimm-scale-7xl': spacing['7xl'],

  // ---- Spacing: numeric aliases ----
  // Ported from the Handover's numeric spacing scale. The ones below that coincide
  // with a named-scale step reference it directly; the rest have no foundation-file
  // source to derive from (not duplicates — genuinely distinct Handover values), so
  // they stay as literals.
  '--zimm-scale-025': '1px',
  '--zimm-scale-200': spacing.xs, // 8px
  '--zimm-scale-300': spacing.s, // 12px
  '--zimm-scale-400': spacing.m, // 16px
  '--zimm-scale-500': spacing.l, // 20px
  '--zimm-scale-600': spacing.xl, // 24px
  '--zimm-scale-700': '28px',
  '--zimm-scale-800': spacing['2xl'], // 32px
  '--zimm-scale-1000': spacing['3xl'], // 40px
  '--zimm-scale-1100': '44px',
  '--zimm-scale-1200': '48px',
  '--zimm-scale-1300': '52px',
  '--zimm-scale-1600': spacing['4xl'], // 64px
  '--zimm-scale-3500': '140px',
  '--zimm-scale-4500': '180px',

  // ---- Spacing: Grid margins ----
  '--zimm-grid-margin-mobile': grid.containerPadding.base,
  '--zimm-grid-margin-tablet': grid.containerPadding.md,
  '--zimm-grid-margin-desktop': grid.containerPadding.xl || '0px',
  // Outer container cap — shared by header/footer/main content. 'none' today; see

  '--zimm-grid-max-width': grid.maxWidth,

  // ---- Spacing: Action sizing ----
  '--zimm-size-action-height-lg': actionSizes.height.lg,
  '--zimm-size-action-height-md': actionSizes.height.md,
  '--zimm-size-action-padding-h-lg': actionSizes.paddingX.lg,
  '--zimm-size-action-padding-h-md': actionSizes.paddingX.md,
  '--zimm-size-action-gap': actionSizes.gap,

  // ---- Border widths ----
  '--zimm-border-width-default': borderWidths.default,

  // ---- Icon sizes ----
  '--zimm-icon-size-xl': iconSizes.xl,
  '--zimm-icon-size-lg': iconSizes.lg,

content.text:
Report delivered to the caller via SubagentHandback, covering all 10 checks with file:line citations, quoted code, and pass/fail/N-A verdicts. Key findings worth highlighting:

- **Check 5 (message↔item association)** and **Check 6 (colour-only for error/success)** came back as genuine FAILs.
- **Check 7a** surfaced a non-obvious, fully-traced finding: the base `QuantityPicker`'s native `disabled` HTML attribute is silently discarded by Chakra's own `Button` component (it overwrites the hook's `disabled` key with its own `isDisabled || isLoading`, which evaluates to `undefined` here) — only `aria-disabled` actually reaches the DOM at a quantity boundary. This required tracing through three Chakra source files (`use-number-input.js`, `button.js`, `styled-system`'s `omitThemingProps`) to confirm rather than assume.
- Also incidentally found that `max` is never passed to the base `QuantityPicker` in the wired component, so the increment boundary is currently unreachable in production — only the `min=0` decrement boundary is live.
- Checks 1, 2, 3, 8, 9, and 10 came back clean/PASS, with Check 4 passing but flagged for a real (narrower-than-wired) forward risk.

All work was read-only — no files edited, no Storybook/Playwright/dev server started.
